headline: Secure Water Access and Camping Permits Early
reservation: Day-use and camping reservations for U.S. Army Corps of Engineers parks, such as Potter's Creek or Comal Park, are essential during peak months. Booking windows vary by site, and popular areas often reach capacity weeks in advance. Always check the official USACE site for current boat ramp status and lake level advisories.

days.title: The Jewel of the Hill Country
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Canyon Lake Marina

stops.name: Canyon Lake Dam
stops.detail: Walk the flat, paved path across the dam for panoramic views of the turquoise water and the Guadalupe River valley below.

stops.name: Overlook Park
stops.detail: Explore the limestone shoreline and find a shaded spot for a lakeside picnic near the dam’s eastern edge.

days.driving: Allow 15–25 minutes; conditions vary by lake traffic
days.note: Limestone surfaces can be slippery when wet; wear shoes with appropriate grip.

days.title: Limestone Bluffs and Hidden Coves

stops.name: Canyon Lake Gorge
stops.detail: Join a scheduled tour to see dinosaur tracks and unique geological formations exposed by historic floodwaters.

stops.name: Madrone Trail
stops.detail: Hike or bike through the oak and cedar brakes on the north shore for views of the central basin.

days.driving: Allow 30–50 minutes; conditions vary on FM 306
days.note: Gorge tours must be booked in advance and are subject to weather-related cancellations.

days.title: River Currents and Historic Gruene

stops.name: Guadalupe River
stops.detail: Visit the tailrace area below the dam, known for being the southernmost trout fishery in the U.S.

stops.name: Gruene Historic District
stops.detail: Drive to nearby New Braunfels to browse Texas’s oldest dance hall and regional boutiques.

days.driving: Allow 45–60 minutes; conditions vary by tourist volume
days.note: River flow rates are controlled by the dam; check USACE release schedules before wading or tubing.

intel.title: Lakeside Parks
intel.text: Parks like Comal and Canyon Park often close to new arrivals by midday on summer Saturdays. Arrive at opening or hold a valid reservation to ensure vehicle entry.

intel.title: Hill Country Coverage
intel.text: Service is generally strong near the main marinas and the dam, but can drop off in the deeper limestone canyons. Download maps for the winding roads on the north side of the lake.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Major fueling stations are located in Startzville and Sattler. Ensure your vessel or vehicle is fueled before entering the more remote park loops.

intel.title: Summer Heat Precautions
intel.text: Plan strenuous hikes for the early morning to avoid peak midday temperatures. The sun reflects intensely off the white limestone, increasing UV exposure.

intel.title: Lake Level Fluctuations
intel.text: Low water levels can result in the closure of specific boat ramps or narrowed swimming areas. Check the official USACE lake level gauges before planning watercraft launches.

plan.arrival: Collect your rental car at SAT and drive north via Hwy 281. Stock up on supplies in New Braunfels or San Marcos before heading to the lake area.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for the region, though an SUV may provide better comfort on the gravel access roads found in some park areas.
plan.goldenHour: Canyon Lake Dam provides an unobstructed view of the western horizon, ideal for sunset over the water during the autumn months.
